A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mid-IR spectra of PAHs in the interstellar medium are a direct probe of the PAH cations to anions ratio.
the astronomical 7.7 and 11.3 μm bands arise from a mixture of small to large compact PAH cations, while the 6.2 and 8.6 features are produced by small and large irregular PAH anions.

large, irregular PAHs are unlikely to be the dominant carriers of the mid-IR emission in the diffuse ISM, while small, compact PAH cations are likely to be the dominant carrier of the 7.6 and 8.6μm emission features.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the astronomical PAH spectra are produced by large compact molecules, not by irregular PAHs.
large irregular PAHs are not important in the interstellar medium, at least not for the emission bands in the 5-9 μm range.
astronomical PAHs are likely compact and not irregular, and the 6.2, 7.7, and 8.6 micron bands are produced by PAH cations while the 11.3 and 12.7 micron bands are produced primarily by PAH anions.
